newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African gold shares finished more than three percent weaker in Friday's quiet trade after bullion slid to 12-year lows, dealers said.

The local gold index which broke through the 1,000 level on June 27, and shed more than three percent at start of trade on Friday in the wake of bullion's overnight slide, finished down 33.1 points or 3.6 percent, at 952.1.
The dealers said the gold market had started sagging late on Thursday on new of Australian central bank gold sales and had remained vulnerable to further losses.
Spot gold late Thursday was down to its lowest levels since early December 1985 when gold was recovering from the low of $281 an ounce seen in February 1985.
"The gold market has been very disappointing today because the gold price is off a lot," Tracy Ledger of stock broking firm BOE Natwest Securites told Reuters.
"The outlook for the golds is uncertain and I will not be buying golds next week. I think a poor gold price set in a very negative (mood) on the market," she added.
dealers said bullion's woes had quickly permeated through the market's gold shares, forcing a majority of them to sink to new year lows.
Among indivual gold shares bullied by bullion's slide were gold mines Driefontein and Western Areas which finished down 115 cents to 59.00 rand and 50 cents to 31.50 rand respectively.
Vaal Reefs closed off 750 cents at 221.00 rand, while Eastvaal ended down 34 cents at 446 cents after the stock earlier dived to a new year low of 418 cents.

"(The slump in the gold price) is not sufficient to knock us off our perch, but I think it's just weakened sentiment for the meantime," said David Shapiro, a director at stock broking firm Societe Generale Frankel Pollak.
Bullion fixed at $324.45 an ounce in London on Friday, making the fix the lowest since late December 1985.
But not only golds took a bashing on Friday in the South African market.
Dealers said industrials followed suit, sagging in sympathy with the precious metal amid some profit-taking following their recent bounce.
Dealers said weakness in the industrial shares was also as a result of some consolidation in a market needing to cool off.
The industrial index ended down 27.9 points at 8,801.9, while the all-share dipped 35.2 points to finish at 7,368.0.
In the broader maket declines led advances by about 223 to 131, while 21 shares hit new highs and 34 slid to new lows.
"The day had been quite quiet with the U.S. closed for the long-weekend and us heading to the weekend as well," Ledger added.
South African Breweries finished unchanged at 140.00 rand, Sasol was down 50 cents at 59.00 rand and Barlows was off 75 cents at 50.00 rand.
Dealers said overall market volumes were moderate with 600 million rand worth of shares exchanging hands at the close.
On the futures side, the South African September industrial contracts finished down on profit-taking, dealers said.
Gold futures were weakened by bullion.
The futures traders said they expected the market to mirror the equities scene and also continue consolidating next week.
The September industrial contract closed at 8,625/29 from 8,688 settlement, golds at 665/70 from 697 settlement and the all-shares contract at 6,758/63 from 6,816.
-- Ellis Mnyandu, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
